body.statement:
Fix an admissible query \(z_0\).  Every labelled point
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\!\left[
 \{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s\}W
 \right]=0
\]
for every cohort \(s\), unit \(i\), and bounded
\(\mathcal X\)-measurable random variable \(W\).  Hence each
\(E\in\mathcal X\) with \(0<\mathbb K_\xi(E)<1\) has treated mean
\(\mu_s\) on both \(E\) and \(E^c\), and
\texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction} excludes the former
common-design-shock kernel.  For each
\(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), these conclusions transfer to its
associated labelled regular conditional point \(\xi_P(z_0)\) for
\(P\)-almost every query \(z_0\), with no assertion at query-null versions.
Nevertheless, there are admissible scalar fixed class parameters and, for
every positive \(N,T,n_1\), two labelled points
\(\xi^{(0)},\xi^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(z_0)\), with causal-data
kernels \(\mathbb K_0,\mathbb K_1\) and corresponding degenerate-query laws
\(P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}\), having the same joint law of
\((X_{1t},Q_{1ti},Z_j)\) and the same target \(\tau(z_0)=0\), while
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_0}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_1}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)
 =\frac1{16}.
\]
Thus removal of the invalid witness is a necessary model repair, not a
determination of the sharp constants for the remaining centered fixed-query
product experiment.
body.justification: The theorem records exactly what centering rules out on the fixed-query class and supplies an explicit two-kernel variance certificate, then transfers the audit to panel laws only almost everywhere.
body.gap: Exact constants for the remaining centered fixed-query optimal-recovery product experiment remain open.
body.consumer: The model audit removes the obsolete negative answer without overstating centering or selecting a null conditional version.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(z_0\) and
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  The bounded-wealth and consistency
clauses of \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class} imply
\(|B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}|\le B\) almost surely, so all expectations below
exist.  The label definition and the design-conditional-centering clause
give
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s\mid\mathcal X]=0.
 \tag{1}
\]
For bounded \(\mathcal X\)-measurable \(W\), the pull-out and tower
properties of conditional expectation yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s)W]
 &=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\!\left[
 W\,\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 (B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s\mid\mathcal X)\right]\\
 &=0.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{2}
\]
This proves the asserted orthogonality.

Let \(E\in\mathcal X\) and set \(p_E=\mathbb K_\xi(E)\).  Taking
\(W=\mathbf 1_E\) in (2) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mathbf 1_E]=\mu_sp_E.
 \tag{3}
\]
If \(p_E>0\), division by \(p_E\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E]=\mu_s.
 \tag{4}
\]
Applying the same argument to \(E^c\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E^c]=\mu_s
 \tag{5}
\]
when \(p_E<1\).  Thus (4)--(5) hold simultaneously when
\(0<p_E<1\), and \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction} supplies the
stated exclusion.  By \texttt{lem:panel-fixed-query-kernel-transfer}, every
\(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) induces a labelled point
\(\xi_P(z_0)\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for almost every query.
Applying (1)--(5) to those points proves the panel-to-kernel transfer and
makes no claim at a null-version query.

We now construct the two labelled points.  For arbitrary positive integers
\(N,T,n_1\), take
\[
 S=1,\quad \pi_1=1,\quad H=0,\quad p=d=1,\quad z_0=\frac12,
 \quad \lambda=\kappa=1,\quad B=L=1,\quad \delta_0=\frac14,
 \tag{6}
\]
and set \(c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), with any fixed \(\beta_0>0\)
and \(\rho_0\in(0,1)\).  These values satisfy all declared parameter
ranges, and \(d=p(H+1)=1\).

On a product probability space let \((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T}\),
\((\eta_j)_{j=1}^{N}\), and \((\varepsilon_i)_{i=1}^{n_1}\) be mutually
independent, with
\[
 X_{1t}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}[0,1],
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(\eta_j=1)=\mathbb P(\eta_j=-1)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(\varepsilon_i=1)=\mathbb P(\varepsilon_i=-1)=\frac12.
 \tag{7}
\]
Define
\[
 m_1(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 Q_{1ti}=m_1(X_{1t})=\frac12,
 \qquad
 Z_j=\frac12+\eta_j.
 \tag{8}
\]
For every event unit set \(W_{1i,-1}=1/2\) and \(R_{1i0}(0)=0\).
Definition \texttt{def:buyhold-level} then gives
\[
 B_{1i}(0)=\frac12.
 \tag{9}
\]
Under \(\mathbb K_0\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=0\); under \(\mathbb K_1\), set
\(R_{1i0}(1)=\varepsilon_i/2\).  In each case impose consistency by setting
\(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{1i}(1)\).  Hence
\[
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\frac12\quad\text{under }\mathbb K_0,
 \qquad
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\frac12+\frac14\varepsilon_i
 \quad\text{under }\mathbb K_1.
 \tag{10}
\]
The smallest constructed return is \(-1/2>-1\), so the return support is
respected.

For \(r\in\{0,1\}\), give \(\mathbb K_r\) the labels
\[
 \mu_1=\frac12,\qquad m_1(x)=\frac12,\qquad \Sigma=1,
 \tag{11}
\]
and call the resulting point \(\xi^{(r)}\).  We verify membership.
Equations (8)--(10) imply
\[
 |Q_{1ti}|=\frac12,
 \qquad |B_{1i}(0)|=\frac12,
 \qquad |B_{1i}(1)|\le\frac34,
 \tag{12}
\]
so bounded wealth holds.  The constant \(m_1\) has supremum norm \(1/2\),
zero derivative, and zero Lipschitz seminorm; hence
\(m_1\in\mathcal H_1(1,1)\).  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}\!\left(\frac12,\partial[0,1]\right)
 =\frac12\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad
 f_{1t\mid z_0}(x)=1
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in[0,1].
 \tag{13}
\]
The design dates are independent, so
\[
 \beta_1(k\mid z_0)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
 \qquad k\ge1.
 \tag{14}
\]

Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T})\).  Training outcomes are
deterministic, and under \(\mathbb K_1\) unit \(i\)'s event history depends
only on \(\varepsilon_i\).  Mutual independence in (7) gives conditional
independence of unit histories across \(i\), while
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_r}[Q_{1ti}\mid\mathcal X]
 =\frac12=m_1(X_{1t}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_r}[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]
 =\frac12=\mu_1.
 \tag{15}
\]
Every \(X_{1t}\) is observed exactly.  The donor sigma-field is generated
by \((\eta_j)_j\), while the joint panel is generated by \((X_{1t})_t\)
and, under \(\mathbb K_1\), \((\varepsilon_i)_i\).  Thus (7) also proves
donor independence from the entire joint panel.

The donor conditions follow from (8):
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_r}Z_j=z_0=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_r}(Z_j)=1=\Sigma,
 \qquad
 c_\Sigma I_1\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_1,
 \tag{16}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_r}
 |\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4
 =\mathbb E|\eta_j|^4=1=B^4.
 \tag{17}
\]
Finally, (9) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_r}B_{1i}(0)=\frac12=m_1(z_0),
 \tag{18}
\]
which is event-date transport, and (10) gives
\(\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_r}B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=1/2=\mu_1\), as required
by the label.  Equations (8)--(18), together with imposed consistency,
verify every clause of \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}.  Therefore
\[
 \xi^{(0)},\xi^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(z_0).
 \tag{19}
\]
If the query variable equals \(1/2\) almost surely and its conditional
causal-data kernel is \(\mathbb K_r\), the resulting law \(P^{(r)}\)
satisfies every member property of \texttt{def:panel-model-class}; the
query-conditional conditions are checked at the sole positive-probability
query.  Hence
\[
 P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)},
 \tag{20}
\]
without selecting a null conditional version.

The joint law of \(((X_{1t})_t,(Q_{1ti})_{t,i},(Z_j)_j)\) is common to
\(\mathbb K_0\) and \(\mathbb K_1\) by (7)--(8).  By
\texttt{def:target}, (9)--(10), and \(\mathbb E\varepsilon_i=0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \tau_{\mathbb K_0}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_0}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)]=0,\\
 \tau_{\mathbb K_1}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_1}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)]
 =\frac14\mathbb E\varepsilon_i=0.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{21}
\]
Nevertheless, (10) and independence of \(\varepsilon_i\) from
\(\mathcal X\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_0}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_1}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)
 =\frac1{16}\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i)=\frac1{16}.
 \tag{22}
\]
Thus the centred labelled class permits different event-noise constants
while holding the training experiment, donor experiment, and causal target
fixed.  This is the claimed explicit certificate.
